QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_44

question.text: For Category I and II AIFs, SEBI's CTR regime prescribes periodic disclosure of the independent valuer's valuation procedure and methodology at what MINIMUM frequency?

answer.text: At least once every six months.
At least once every five years.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 12 (CTR Table 12.1, 'Calculation of NAV'): 'The description of Valuation procedure and methodology adopted by an independent valuer shall be disclosed in the periodic reporting by Category I and II AIFs which shall be at least once in every six months.' The Trap: Daily is the Cat III mechanic — classic trap. Monthly is tighter than AIF norms. Every 5 years matches record retention, not valuation frequency. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C identical. XIX-B Cat III distributor exam drills daily NAV (which belongs to Cat III only). Do not transplant Cat III daily NAV onto Cat I/II. Manager's Pro-Tip: Align valuer rotation with the half-yearly disclosure: engage each valuer for 2 cycles max, rotate thereafter. LPs view long-tenure valuer relationships as governance weakness.
